picks.title: Apple is working on a way to authenticate that a photo came from an iPhone camera
picks.excerpt: References included in iOS 27 beta 5 point to a new feature designed to authenticate the camera source of an iPhone photo.
picks.rationale: Capture-source provenance baked into the phone everyone shoots with — the first practical answer to 'is this image real?' inside a creative team's asset pipeline.

picks.title: Meta’s latest AI model wants to live on your PC
picks.excerpt: Meta’s Muse Glimmer is a 30B AI model made to run locally on your PC.
picks.rationale: A 30B model targeted at ordinary workstations pulls confidential design work off the cloud and onto the machine already on the desk.

picks.title: This 'adversarial' pattern can prevent surveillance cameras from detecting you
picks.excerpt: A security researcher has designed an algorithm that can create computer-generated patterns capable of hiding people, faces, and vehicles from detection by surveillance cameras.
picks.rationale: Surface pattern as a functional defence against machine vision — graphic design turned into an anti-detection layer, with a generator anyone can run.

picks.title: HoverAir unveils the Versa modular pocket gimbal camera that transforms into a self-flying drone
picks.title_note: Modular camera transforms into an auto-tracking drone by magnetically snapping together for instant palm launch and AI tracking
picks.rationale: One magnetic module turns a pocket gimbal into an auto-tracking drone — a two-in-one capture rig that removes a whole camera operator from small shoots.

picks.title: Home Assistant automations finally read like plain English
picks.excerpt: Intent-based triggers replace years of automation guesswork.
picks.rationale: Intent-based triggers replace brittle device-state logic — a hands-on account of automations becoming readable, which is exactly how AI should change tooling.
